title: Pool latency regression: signal hunt and isolation notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working notes from the on-call signal hunt for the dedicated GPU pool latency regression observed on 2024-11-14 -> 2024-11-15. This is an informal working doc: hypotheses, commands run, temporary mitigations, and a first-draft isolation checklist that we can formalize into a runbook if validated.

Executive summary (short):
- Between ~2024-11-14 02:10 UTC and 2024-11-14 06:30 UTC we saw repeated p95/p99 token latency spikes for customers on gpu-pool-4 (us-west-2a).
- Impact: elevated tail latency for 3 dedicated customer pools (two small, one medium). No API auth issues or model corruption detected.
- Temporary mitigation: moved two noisy workloads off pool-4 to pool-8 (same region) at 06:50 UTC which immediately reduced the p99 for affected customer routes.
- Current working hypothesis: a tenant-internal workload pattern causing KV-cache thrash + inefficient attention window usage (long context + frequent checkpointing) amplified by a kernel scheduling artifact on 80GB A100 that increases per-token latency when GPU sm utilization is saturated while PCIe transfers spike.

Timeline and important signals (local time UTC):
- 2024-11-14 02:03 — First automated alert: p99 token latency for pool-gpu-4 route "gen-large" exceeded 1.2s (alert threshold 600ms).
- 02:05 — Oncall (Asha) paged; opened JIRA-ENG-4821.
- 02:10 — Checked pool metrics dashboard: GPU util 72-95% with large instantaneous spikes; P2-to-host PCIe retransmits elevated on two nodes (node-4a-03, node-4a-05).
- 02:18 — Looked at request distribution: 60% of requests had context length > 10k tokens for one customer (cust-eta).
- 02:35 — K/V cache hit ratio dropped for the pool; cache fill/evict churn increased.
- 03:00 — Attempted a soft-nudge: throttled cust-eta at the router layer to 70% of prior QPS for 15 minutes — minor improvement, but spikes persisted.
- 04:45 — Correlated with infra: a background backup job on nodes node-4a-05 initiated large NVMe reads (internal infra job).
- 05:12 — Hypothesis refined: simultaneous long-context workloads + NVMe/PCIe contention -> kernel scheduling latency bump.
- 06:50 — We moved cust-eta and a second noisy tenant to pool-8; p99 dropped to baseline within ~6 minutes.

What we checked (commands / dashboards):
- Metrics dashboards: p95/p99 token latency per pool, per-route QPS, GPU util per node, mem alloc and KV cache hit/miss, PCIe error/retransmit rates, NVMe IOps.
- node logs: /var/log/syslog and dmesg for kernel preempt warnings, PCIe AER messages.
- Serving runtime traces: per-request tail metrics (time spent: prefill, sampling, kernel execution, host copy).
- Router level: rate limit decisions, tenant routing logs to confirm which nodes served noisy requests.
- kubectl/top and nvidia-smi sampling across nodes to check SM utilization and memory clocks.

Quick reproduction attempts (notes):
- Replaying representative request from cust-eta against a single node VM in staging with 12k token context reproduced increased host copy times and cache churn, but not full-blown latency spike unless a synthetic NVMe read load was added (fio -rw randread).
- Adding NVMe load to staging node while running long-context generation created a similar p99 amplification.

Immediate mitigations applied (temporary):
- Tenant routing: moved noisy tenants off pool-4 to pool-8 (completed 06:50 UTC).
- Router-level soft throttles on heavy-context routes for 60 minutes following migration.
- Added short-term alert: watch PCIe retransmits > 100/min for any node (to catch recurrence).

First-draft isolation checklist (for oncall):
1) Confirm p99/p95 deviation and affected pools via Pool Latency Dashboard.
2) Identify top 3 routes by contribution to p99 (group by tenant/route).
3) Check per-node SM util / mem clock / NVMe IO; flag nodes with NVMe busy > 80% or PCIe retransmit spikes.
4) If single tenant dominates, attempt router-level QPS cap to 50% for 10m and watch latency.
5) If latency persists, migrate tenant to another pool (prefer different rack/host family).
6) If multiple tenants involved and hardware IO signals high, consider cordon-and-drain of most affected node(s) and schedule node reprovision; follow eviction policy for dedicated pools.
7) Record actions with timestamps in incident Jira and Slack thread #sre-ops.

Root-cause hypotheses (candidates):
- Hypothesis A (primary): tenant workload pattern (long context + low batching) interacts poorly with our KV cache and causes persistent host<->device transfers; when NVMe/PCIe background IO is high, host copy latency amplifies tail.
- Hypothesis B: a regression in the serving runtime kernel selection path that on certain SM util distributions picks a suboptimal kernel leading to increased latency when memory copies are in flight. (recent PR: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/1098 touched kernel chooser)
- Hypothesis C: localized NVMe controller firmware hiccup on node-4a-05 leading to elevated IO latency under concurrent loads.

Longer-term follow-ups and action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Asha: capture a reproducible staging scenario and produce a minimal repro (due 2024-11-22).
- Ben: run targeted NVMe firmware audit on node-4a-03/05 and coordinate with infra for flash vendor (due 2024-11-26).
- Lina: add a new synthetic check that exercises long-context KV-cache churn + NVMe background IO to our chaos tests (due 2024-12-05).
- Mateo: review kernel selection PRs from last 30 days and add a microbenchmark to catch regressions affecting long-token streams (due 2024-11-29).
- SRE team: evaluate eviction thresholds and routing fallback rules (draft a policy by 2024-12-10).

Runbook draft additions (to be reviewed and formalized):
- New signal to add: KV cache evict-churn rate (evictions/min) per pool. Threshold: > 300 evict/min for > 5m -> escalates.
- Hardware signal: PCIe retransmit > 50/min -> page to infra-as-a-service + SRE.
- Router policy: auto-fallback to lower-cost pooling if a tenant's median context length > 6k tokens and p99 > 800ms for 5m.
- Migration guidance: prefer target pools in different rack to avoid shared NVMe controller contention.

Unresolved questions (for post-incident RCA):
- What changed 48-72 hours prior? any batch infra job schedule changes or tenant-side software push? (ask ownership: platform-ops / cust-eta eng)
- How often do kernel-selection regressions surface only under combined IO+long-context patterns vs pure compute saturation?
- Should we add soft isolation throttles specifically for long-context routes by default?

Notes & artifacts collected (links):
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-4821 (incident thread, timeline, owners)
- Grafana: pool-latency-dashboard (panel ids: toproutes, per-node-gpu-telemetry)
- Staging repro workspace: github.com/redwood/repro-cases/long-context-io
- Slack thread: #sre-ops (thread ts: 1700000000.000000)

Appendix: useful commands run during hunt (copy/paste friendly)
- tail -n 200 /var/log/syslog | grep -i pcie
- dmesg | egrep "AER|I/O error|timeout"
- kubectl -n serving get pods -o wide --selector=pool=gpu-4
- nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 5 (sampled across nodes)
- curl -s "https://grafana.internal/pool-latency?var-pool=gpu-4&panel=toproutes" | jq .
- fio --name=bgread --rw=randread --bs=128k --size=10G --iodepth=32 --filename=/dev/nvme0n1

Final thoughts:
This felt like an emergent coupling of workload shape (long-context tenants), background IO (NVMe backups / infra jobs), and a scheduling/serving runtime sensitivity that only shows up as a tail amplification. The migration immediate improvement is a strong signal that tenant shaping + routing fallback policy will buy us breathing room until we have either a runtime fix or hardware mitigation.

Next sync: informal RCA/working session planned 2024-11-21 16:00 UTC in #sre-ops; please bring checkpoints (staging repro, kernel-picker review, NVMe vendor notes).

(End of notes)
